dod_intent_evidence: Completed a $1.9M US Army SBIR Phase II ('Terahertz Sensing for Situation Awareness') per SBIR.gov and PRNewswire coverage, and own-language homepage lists 'defend and secure our troops' among served industries, with active 'Director of Business Development - Defense' and 'Customer Engineer - Defense' job postings.
score_evidence: '0.13° native resolution... 20x better than leading automotive imaging radars' → lab_language_intensity

'first A sample sensor system developed' / 'First B Sample sensor expected' / 'Mass Production Sensor Ready for vehicle programs' (2028) roadmap with zero DDIL/ATO/RMF/CMMC/ITAR mention → deployment_awareness_absence
'help defend and secure our troops' is the only operator-adjacent phrase in ~1300 words; no mention of training, CONOPS, or field feedback → operator_absence

'Customer Engineer - Defense' and 'Director of Business Development - Defense' postings show some field/customer-facing defense hiring, offsetting an otherwise research/silicon-heavy roster → hiring_profile_skew

blind_spots.blind_spot: Spec-sheet metrics (resolution, range) with no ruggedization or SWaP-C framing for a vehicle-mounted defense sensor
blind_spots.operator_reality: A terahertz sensor rated for automotive ADAS conditions is not automatically survivable on a tactical vehicle platform — dust, vibration, thermal extremes, and power budget on a mounted military vehicle are a different environment than a passenger car.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Company's core business and hiring (DSP, silicon packaging, radar systems engineers) is automotive-first; defense is framed as an adjacent market, not a co-designed use case.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: '0.13° native resolution... 20x better than leading automotive imaging radars'

blind_spots.blind_spot: Product roadmap shows no field pilot with military operators before 2028 mass production
blind_spots.operator_reality: Without an operator-facing pilot, there is no training, CONOPS, or sustainment plan being built in parallel with the hardware — by the time the sensor is field-ready, the SBIR-funded advocacy window may have closed.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Roadmap is entirely hardware-maturity milestones (chip → array → A/B/C sample → mass production), with no parallel deployment or operator-integration milestone listed.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: '2028 Mass Production Sensor Ready for vehicle programs'

blind_spots.blind_spot: No ATO/RMF/CMMC/ITAR/STIG language despite an active Army threat-detection contract
blind_spots.operator_reality: A sensor feeding 'battlefield situation awareness' will eventually need to pass data into a government network or platform — without ATO/RMF groundwork started now, the transition from SBIR Phase II demo to a program of record stalls on compliance, not technology.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Own-language and job postings are entirely hardware/silicon-engineering focused; no compliance, ISSO, or government-integration role is posted.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: 'The goal of the $1,899,778 contract is to deploy new terahertz sensing capabilities to heighten battlefield situation awareness and protect U.S. and allied troops.'

opener_hook: Teradar completed its $1.9M Army SBIR Phase II for battlefield terahertz threat detection in March 2026, with mass-production sensors not slated on the public roadmap until 2028.
what_they_do: Solid-state terahertz imaging sensors for all-weather vehicle vision, sold primarily into automotive ADAS with a secondary defense/battlefield sensing line.
